item.text:
Turn complete. Report updated at [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_14-01-25-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md).

This turn I converted Finding 1 from a well-evidenced diagnosis into a causally validated one, without touching the captured implementation.

I copied the root module to a scratch directory (`work/fixcheck/`) and applied only the one-line fix there — re-assigning the reference peer set inside `EnsureSamePeers`' retry loop:

```go
WAIT:
	c.WaitEvent(nil, c.conf.CommitTimeout)
	peerSet = c.getConfiguration(c.rafts[0])   // the missing refresh
	goto CHECK
```

Same conditions, 20 iterations each:

| test | unmodified `work/` | fixed `work/fixcheck/` |
|---|---|---|
| `TestRaft_ProtocolVersion_Upgrade_2_3` | 6/20 fail | 0/20 fail |
| `TestRaft_HasExistingState` | 4/20 fail | 0/20 fail |

That single missing re-assignment is therefore both necessary and sufficient for the flakiness, and it confirms the root cause is the frozen reference in the test helper rather than anything in the Raft protocol or state machine.

I also verified the captured tree is untouched: `diff -rq source work` reports no differing files — only my additions appear (`report.md`, `audit-evidence/`, `fixcheck/`, `repro/`, and the `zz_audit_*` diagnostics), and `source/testing.go` is byte-identical to `work/testing.go`.

Evidence logs are preserved durably in `work/audit-evidence/` (including the two new comparison logs), and the report's Finding 1 section now includes this validation table.

Final state: one confirmed defect (Finding 1 in `testing.go`), causally validated with a minimal fix; no consensus-level defect found by source review plus five independent behavioral methods (~16k acked commands); and the one honest open question — whether the missing refresh line is the injected mutation or a latent upstream flake — remains unanswerable offline for lack of a trustworthy upstream reference.
